title: And I heard the voice of that Egyptian highpriest
html_source:
From John F Taylor’s speech at the Law Student Debating Society, 24th October 1901. Taylor was a King’s Counsel and spoke in defence of the Irish language. This was part of the general movement against the Anglicisation of Ireland. The speech was part of the nationalist hubbub in Chapter 7 of Ulysses (Aeolus episode).

The speech concludes with Taylor telling how an Egyptian high priest compared their mighty achievements to the lowly language and culture of Jews. Taylor finishes with ‘ ‘If Moses had listened to the counsels of that learned Professor he would never have come down from the mountain, his face glowing as a star, and bearing the Tables of the Law…’
(James Joyce Centre).

Joyce, with the help of his ally, Sylvia Beach made a recording of a version of the speech published by the nationalist Roger Casement in 1924.
